'''''Encalypta streptocarpa''''', the '''spiral extinguisher-moss''', is a species of moss.<ref name="bbs">{{cite web |title=Encalypta streptocarpa |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/encalypta-streptocarpa/ |publisher=British Bryological Society |access-date=5 February 2026}}</ref><ref name="bbsfield2010">{{cite book |title=Mosses and Liverworts of Britain and Ireland: a Field Guide |date=2010 |publisher=British Bryological Society |page=557 |edition=1 |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Encalypta-streptocarpa.pdf |access-date=5 February 2026}}</ref>

==Morphology==
The broad, dull green leaves are unique in the genus for the nerve does not reach the leaf tip. ''E. streptocarpa'' often lacks capsules. [[Calyptra]] are large and distinguish the moss from members of the [[Pottiales]], otherwise similar, such as ''[[Tortula subulata]]''.<ref name="bbsfield2010"/>

==Reproduction==
''Encalypta streptocarpa'' is notable in rarely producing spores; instead it disperses by gemmae, visible as small orange bright grows in the moss.<ref name="bbs"/>

==Habitat==
This species is a [[calcicole]], most easily found on [[limestone]] and calcareous rocks. However it can grow on several different substrates, such as [[sandstone]], [[igneous rocks]], [[chalk]] soil to [[beech]] roots in woods. Artificial environments include mortar and limestone surfaces, especially crumbling ones. It prefers good lighting rather than deep shade and it is found from [[sea level]] up to 650 meters.<ref name="bbsatlas2014">{{cite book |title=Atlas of British and Irish Bryophytes (vol.1) |date=2014 |publisher=Pisces Publications |location=Newbury |isbn=9781874357612 |page=434 |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Atlas-of-British-and-Irish-Bryophytes-V1-434.pdf |access-date=26 March 2026}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Widespread in Europe, including Iceland and Scandinavia. It is found eastward up to the [[Ural Mountains]]. It has been reported also from the [[Canary Islands]], [[Turkey]], [[Syria]], [[Morocco]], [[Caucasus]] and [[Iran]].<ref name="bbsatlas2014"/>
